The stale copy ocmsadminprivateapi/cronservice/ is not used as evidence
note: Status 'Requirement given - Gen flow'; demo_remark: 'Internet PII encryption - cannot fetch offender particulars'. There is no flow deck and Appendix B Annex 1A is not in the repo. This is the twin of OCMS11.46 (NOPO) for the Payment Evasion epic; the code is the same so the fits are kept equal. The furnish flow exists end to end: the e-service validates furnishable notices (stages ROV, ENA, RD1, RD2), saves a pending application in the Internet PII DB, the SyncInternetIntranet job (enabled=true in PROD, every 10 minutes) pulls it and runs auto-approval or manual review, then the driver becomes the offender and the notice moves to DN1 (a furnished hirer goes to RD1). Stage RR3 and above cannot be furnished. Gaps proven from the repo: the hirer's notice lookup depends on DecryptByKey in the PII DB (as in the demo_remark; cannot verify from repo), Appendix B is not in the repo, and the DN1 letter to the driver does not reach Toppan because the SFTP upload is blocked in application-prod.properties:86 while the stage still advances (OCMS-DF-2026-192, Ready to UAT). Tickets OCMS-DF-2026-170 and -024 (Closed) touch the stage change and the address after furnish; -110, -143, -175 are submit errors (Closed).
recommendation: Claim partially. The furnish flow up to the driver becoming the offender and entering stage DN1 exists in code. Ask URA for proof that the PII lookup in the Internet DB works in PRD, for confirmation of Appendix B, and for when the Toppan upload block is lifted, before a full claim

steps.step: The hirer opens the Furnish Driver's Particulars e-service and looks up the outstanding notices under their name
steps.detail: The furnish-particulars route exists in ocmseserviceui (route.ts:38-42). In the API, findFurnishableNoticeNos picks notices with offender_indicator='Y' and owner_driver_indicator <> 'D', so a hirer (H) or owner (O) passes but a driver does not (EocmsOffenceNoticeOwnerDriverRepository.java:71-80, used by FurnishValidationServiceImpl.java:253-263: F07 if not the offender, F08 if a driver). The query reads id_no through DecryptByKey on the PII DB; the symmetric key is opened in EocmsOffenceNoticeOwnerDriverServiceImpl.java:43-46 and 143-150. This story's demo_remark says exactly 'Internet PII encryption - cannot fetch offender particulars'. Whether the key, certificate, and permission are correct in Azure cannot verify from repo, so Sebagian. Same fit as OCMS11.46.

steps.step: Furnishing is only open at the pre-defined processing stages (ROV, ENA, 1st reminder RD1, 2nd reminder RD2)
steps.detail: isProcessingStageEligible lets a notice through if last_processing_stage is in ELIGIBLE_STAGES = ROV, ENA, RD1, RD2, or (fallback) next_processing_stage is in RD1, RD2 (FurnishValidationServiceImpl.java:175-183; SystemConstant.java:112-113). In getIneligibilityReason a stage outside that is rejected with FURNISH_NOTICE_STAGE_INELIGIBLE (FurnishValidationServiceImpl.java:210-213). This matches the story's example (1st and 2nd reminder); a newly furnished hirer starts at RD1 so passes through these stages. Suspended notices (crs_reason), PS-DIP/MID/FOR/RIP/RP2, and UPL are also rejected (FurnishValidationServiceImpl.java:189-208). Appendix B Annex 1A is not in the repo. Same fit as OCMS11.46.

steps.step: The hirer fills in the driver's particulars and submits; the application is saved with status pending
steps.detail: The UI maps the answer to Q1 'Was the person the driver...' to ownerDriverIndicator: Yes becomes D (driver), No becomes H (hirer); a UEN is always H (MapFurnish.ts:43, 111; HDQuests.ts:36-38). POST /v1/furnishapplication runs validation, then submitFurnishApplication creates one txn_no per notice, moves the supporting documents, and saves EocmsFurnishApplication with the request's owner_driver_indicator and status pending to the PII DB (FurnishSubmissionController.java:66-70; FurnishSubmissionServiceImpl.java:43, 187, 210). Tickets OCMS-DF-2026-110, -143 and -175 (all Closed) reported errors on submit; -175 was closed with no code change as a temporary service condition. Same fit as OCMS11.46.

steps.step: The submission is moved to the staff system and checked automatically; failures go to manual officer review
steps.detail: SyncInternetIntranetJobsScheduler runs FurnishProcessingJob (SyncInternetIntranetJobsScheduler.java:47-67); cron.syncinternetintranet.enabled=true with a 10-minute schedule in PROD (cron-schedules-prod.properties:305-306). FurnishProcessingService calls executeApproval when all checks pass, or executeManualReview with a reason otherwise (FurnishProcessingService.java:160-176). Six checks: active permanent suspension, HST ID, FIN/passport, stage still furnishable (LPS|NPS pairs in SystemConstant.java:237-244), existing offender, and prior submission (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:183-225, 319-337). Note: OCMS11.46 cites cron-schedules-prod.properties:292, which is the syncintranetinternet property (the opposite direction); the property this scheduler reads is syncinternetintranet at lines 305-306. The real PROD server value cannot verify from repo.

steps.step: The furnished driver becomes the current offender on the notice and the hirer is no longer the offender
steps.detail: executeApproval calls addFurnishedOffender (adds an ocms_offence_notice_owner_driver row for the furnished person, including a furnished_mail address flagged letter_address Y) and changeProcessingStage; switchOffenderIndicator lowers the old offender's indicator from Y to N in both the Intranet and Internet DB (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:445-466, 542-641, 713-748). Ticket OCMS-DF-2026-024 (Closed, prod) concerns the old driver's mha_reg address after a furnish overwrite; the current code is not re-proven here. Same fit as OCMS11.46.

steps.step: The notice enters the driver follow-up track (stage DN1) according to the automated workflow in Appendix B of Annex 1A
steps.detail: changeProcessingStage: when the furnished party's indicator is D, last/next_processing_stage becomes DN1 (H becomes RD1), the previous stage is kept, the admin fee is zeroed and amount_payable is reset to composition_amount, next_processing_date = max(notice_date + 7 days, tomorrow), then the Internet VON is synced (FurnishApprovalHelper.java:644-710). Appendix B Annex 1A is not in the repo, so whether the 7-day rule and stage order match that document cannot verify from repo. Ticket OCMS-DF-2026-170 (Closed, prod) was a wrong $15 admin fee on DN1->DN1 and RD1->RD1 transitions, patched at FurnishApprovalHelper.java:668-675. Same fit as OCMS11.46.

steps.step: The driver receives the next follow-up (a DN1 letter through the print vendor) according to the workflow
steps.detail: Stage DN1 exists in ToppanStage (ToppanStage.java:22) and is processed by the Toppan cron (ToppanLettersGeneratorJob.java:151); notices are picked by next_processing_stage=DN1 with offender_indicator='Y' and no suspension (OcmsValidOffenceNoticeRepository.java:608-612), so the one who is sent the letter is the driver. But application-prod.properties:86 blocks the SFTP upload to Toppan (sftp.upload.disabledServers=toppan), the daily generation call is commented out (ToppanUploadJobsScheduler.java:118), and the stage still advances because the gate is bypassed (ToppanUploadJob.java:424-430). Ticket OCMS-DF-2026-192 (Ready to UAT) discusses this. The real PROD server state cannot verify from repo. Same fit as OCMS11.46 (delivery to the vendor).
